rationale: I own Allstate, and the numbers still justify it. A P/E of 7.08 against 17.07% five-year earnings growth gives a PEG of 0.41, well inside my strong-buy zone, and debt-to-equity of 0.22 is clean. The 19.01% gain in about six months is nowhere near the 30-50% in one to two years where I'd start thinking about selling a Stalwart, and I don't cut flowers to water weeds. What keeps me from adding with abandon is that a P/E of 7 on an insurer can mean peak-cycle earnings, and this snapshot gives me no 3-year growth, free cash flow, margin or insider data to rule that out. I make no intrinsic value estimate because the inputs aren't there. I hold, and I watch whether growth holds up and the multiple stays this cheap.
